chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Ḥumayd ibn Ziyād, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, from more than one person, from Abān, from Abī Maryam, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: "If the martyr still has some life in him, he is given ghusl, shrouded, perfumed with ḥanūṭ, and salat is performed over him. But if there is no life left in him, he is buried in his clothes."

key_terms.أَثْوَابِهِ: his clothes, meaning the garments he was wearing
key_terms.الشَّهِيدُ: the martyr; one killed in the path of Allah whose burial rulings are discussed here
key_terms.حُنِّطَ: he was perfumed with funeral camphor preparation
key_terms.رَمَقٌ: a remaining trace of life or last breath
key_terms.صُلِّيَ عَلَيْهِ: the funeral salat was performed over him
key_terms.غُسِّلَ: he was given ghusl (ritual washing of the deceased)
key_terms.كُفِّنَ: he was shrouded in a burial cloth

ai.seo_question: What are the funeral rulings for a martyr in Shia Islam if he is still alive after being wounded?
ai.summary: This hadith states the ruling for a martyr at the time of death and burial. If he still shows signs of life, the normal funerary rites are performed for him; if he has no remaining life, he is buried in his clothes. The narration is significant in fiqh for distinguishing funeral rulings based on whether life remained after injury.
